items.title: Open v2.86.0 and land library-stack-§7's narrowed `__` clause (precondition for OptionsTabs minor 9)
items.spec:
Opens the ONE standard version of this run, v2.86.0 (OWNER_SCOPE B). Every later WS item appends a ruling paragraph to this entry and never bumps again. Two LibKa0s items wait on this one: (a) the #45 item that removes O.__releaseChrome (OptionsTabs minor 8 -> 9, LibKa0s/OptionsTabs.lua:51 TABS_MINOR = 8), because the clause must exist before or with that removal; (b) the v1.75.0 release item, because LibKa0s docs/releasing.md:117 checks its README pointer against `head -1 ../WowAddonStandards/standards/STANDARDS.md`.

Baseline: master 6bb1bc7 (v2.85.0, 2026-10-20). `bash scripts/check-standard.sh` exits 0 there (7 checks; anti-patterns #1-#95; 27 section files). Create the run branch `feat/2026-10-22-libka0s-issues-45-58` from it. This is a documents-only repo: no Lua, no CCN and no 1500-line cap. Its gate is check-standard.sh, LF only, and a read for meaning (CLAUDE.md 'Editing rules').

End state:
1. **Version and changelog.**
   - standards/STANDARDS.md:1 reads `# Ka0s WoW Addon Standard (v2.86.0, <D>)`, where D is the day this item commits. WS-11 re-stamps every place if the run lands later.
   - The v2.85.0 bullet at STANDARDS.md:100 moves VERBATIM to the top of standards/CHANGELOG.md's list, above the v2.84.0 bullet at :5.
   - STANDARDS.md '## Changelog' holds one new bullet, `- **v2.86.0 (<D>):** **Rulings from the LibKa0s #45–#58 run.**`, carrying three parts. First, a lead paragraph naming the run (Ka0sAddonsCommonTasks docs/2026-10-22-LIBKA0S_ISSUES_45_58). Second, the ruling paragraph `**library-stack-§7: a documented-internal `__` member with no consumer is not contract.**` with the first removal. Third, the closing lines `Version rippled to CLAUDE.md, README.md, EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md and NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md.` and `Minor.` The 'Full history' line stays.
   - Later items insert their ruling paragraphs above the ripple line.
2. **Version stamps.** check-standard's version-stamps check reads five places, and all of them must agree in this commit:
   - README.md:173: `The standard is at **v2.86.0**`.
   - CLAUDE.md:172: `As of v2.86.0 the sets are:`. The doc sets themselves are unchanged.
   - standards/EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md:11: `current: **v2.86.0**, <D>`.
   - standards/NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md:1: `(v2.86.0, <D>)`.
   - docs/ARCHITECTURE.md carries no stamp. Confirm with grep.
3. **The narrowed clause.** This text binds over design-std A11.1. Insert a new bullet in standards/standards/library-stack.md, directly after the additive-only MUST at :116. Its sense:
   - A `__`-prefixed member that the library documents as internal (an attach seam such as `lib.__AttachTabs`, a minor probe its suites read such as `__tabsMinor`) or as a test seam **MAY** be removed in a later minor, once it has **zero roster consumers** and nothing in the payload, the library's suites, tests/majors.lua or the testkit reaches it. The file's minor moves, and the CHANGELOG names the removal.
   - A documented `__` member that consumers call **remains contract** under the additive-only MUST: `__PatchLSM30Border`, `__IsCombatLocked`, `__AttachCompose`, `__panels` and the like.
   - A library-absent stub that mirrors a removed member for surface parity is dead. Kit.assertSurfaceParity reads live keys only, so such a stub stays green. It is deleted in the consumer's next re-vendor commit.
   - The testkit is not a LibStub major, and this rule does not reach it. A kit member listed in a kit version document is the kit's contract to consumer suites, whatever its name. Example: `M.__fireUnconditional`, which slash-commands-§7 step 6 is built on.
   - The first removal is `O.__releaseChrome` (OptionsTabs minor 9, LibKa0s v1.75.0, LibKa0s#45). It is no precedent for removing a public member.
   - **Do NOT** write design-std's sentence 'A consumer MUST NOT call a `__` member'. Consumers call these today. The roster grep outside libs/ and tests/_kit/ (run 2026-10-22) found `__PatchLSM30Border` in 12 files, `__panels` in 26, `__AttachCompose` in 4 and `__IsCombatLocked` in 1. `__releaseChrome` appears in 9 files, all of them the dead stub mirrors.
4. **Index blurb.** STANDARDS.md:57, the library-stack blurb: append '; a documented-internal `__` member with no consumer is removable in a later minor, while one that consumers call stays contract'.
5. **AUDIT.md**, in the LibKa0s vendoring checks near :496: add one bullet. A library-absent stub still mirroring a `__` member that the bundled tag removed is a finding (library-stack-§7). It is dead and is removed at re-vendor. A consumer call to a documented, live `__` member is NOT a finding.

No new anti-pattern, no section heading, and no script change.

Commit: `WS-01: open v2.86.0; library-stack-§7 narrows the __ clause (LibKa0s#45)`, with the session trailers.

Verify (from Ka0sAddonsCommonTasks):
```
cd ../WowAddonStandards
bash scripts/check-standard.sh                      # exit 0; version-stamps reports v2.86.0 in all places
head -1 standards/STANDARDS.md                      # v2.86.0
grep -c 'v2.85.0 (2026-10-20)' standards/CHANGELOG.md   # 1, and it sits above v2.84.0
grep -n '__releaseChrome\|__PatchLSM30Border' standards/standards/library-stack.md   # the clause
grep -n 'MUST NOT call a `__`' -r standards AUDIT.md  # nothing
for f in $(git diff --name-only HEAD~1); do tr -dc '\r' < $f | wc -c; done   # all 0
git log -1 --format=%s | grep -q '^WS-01: '
```

items.title: launcher-§6 (MUST): the Show window key binding on the toggle handler; layout-§1 Bindings.xml generalized; slash-commands-§7 key press; anti-pattern #96; playbook and pack ripple
items.spec:
Implements design-std A1-A3, A6 (#96 only) and A14, with OWNER_SCOPE F's corrections binding over them.

Corrections that differ from the design:
- (i) The section body does **not** enumerate addons. Drop 'At v2.86.0 that is six addons…' and the bullet list under it. ADDONS.md's Show window column is the list. STANDARDS.md:43 forbids naming a reference implementation in normative text, so describe the existing binding instead of naming it.
- (ii) The refusal is 'refuses exactly as the toggle does', which follows from calling the same handler. The by-hold choice of line stays the **SHOULD** it already is in slash-commands-§7 *Which refusal, by hold* (slash-commands.md:280-295). It is not upgraded to a MUST here.

End state:

1. **standards/standards/launcher.md**
   - **§2, the bullet 'Clicking an entry toggles it through the addon's OWN handler' (:55).** After '…or the display's `toggle` verb.', add: 'That same handler is what the addon's Show window key binding presses (launcher-§6). The menu entry, the `toggle` verb and the key are three surfaces onto one handler.'
   - **New heading after §5 (file end, :112): `### 6. The Show window key binding (MUST)`.** Content, from design-std A1 minus the enumeration:
     - An addon whose launcher has a Show window entry (launcher-§2; its ADDONS.md row) MUST ship one key binding that toggles that window or display.
     - **One binding, one handler.** A `CLICK <Folder>Toggle<Window>:LeftButton` binding in the root Bindings.xml (layout-§1), with `header="<FOLDERUPPER>"` on the file's first Binding only and `category="ADDONS"`. It names a plain, named, hidden, non-secure Button that a module creates at load, registered with `RegisterForClicks("AnyDown")`. Its OnClick calls **the handler the descriptor's `toggleWindow` calls**. Not allowed: a second handler or a global function; Lua in the Binding element; a secure template. Include the XML snippet.
     - **The button name is permanent.** Renaming it silently unbinds every player's key.
     - **Labels.** `BINDING_HEADER_<FOLDERUPPER>` = `Ka0s <Name>` (launcher-§1). The `BINDING_NAME_CLICK <button>:LeftButton` label comes through L. Both are assigned in the module that creates the button, the second via rawset.
     - **No default key.** Bindings.xml MUST NOT carry a `default` attribute.
     - **A press while stood down refuses exactly as the toggle does (MUST).** It calls the toggle's handler, so it toggles nothing and writes nothing while the addon is stood down (slash-commands-§7). It answers with the line the `toggle` verb answers with. Where the handler relies on the dispatcher's gate rather than refusing itself, the button's OnClick asks the addon's one refusal helper first, so the press and the verb cannot differ. Which line is printed is slash-commands-§7 *Which refusal, by hold*: a SHOULD there, unchanged here. Its existing MUST NOT, never the disabled line under the perf hold alone, binds the press like any refusal site. A silent press where the verb would print is a finding.
     - **Combat.** A press adds no combat contract of its own.
     - **Documented.** README '## Usage' names the binding and where to set it (Key Bindings → AddOns → `Ka0s <Name>`). docs/settings-panel.md's launcher row lists it.
     - **Why this is not a library helper (recorded rejection, LibKa0s#58).** Keep the design's four reasons and its re-check trigger: two or more rollout buttons diverge on correctness, or a second binding per addon is ruled in. Add that the kit `test_bindings` check is deferred.
     - **Commencement.** Each owing addon's next release. Anti-pattern #96.
   - **§5.** Append the fourth-adoption paragraph from design-std A1: it needs no library tag; per owing addon, create the button and labels in the module owning the toggle, add the CLICK line to a root Bindings.xml (layout-§1), extend tests/test_disabled.lua step 8, and document it.

2. **standards/standards/layout.md**
   - **:12-13 tree comment** → `Bindings.xml -- key bindings: owed by every addon with a Show window entry (launcher-§6), else ONLY if the addon ships bindings; …` (design-std A2 wording).
   - **:101.** 'a `CLICK` binding on a secure button needs none at all' → 'a `CLICK` binding on a named button needs none at all, whether the button is secure or the plain hidden button every Show window binding presses (launcher-§6)'. Replace 'An addon with no key bindings has no such file.' with the A2 sentence.
   - **:103.** Append the A2 sentence, without the 'six repositories' count. Say 'every addon whose launcher has a Show window entry'.

3. **standards/standards/slash-commands.md**
   - **:295 'Every refusal site uses one helper'.** 'A feature verb, a button press, a key binding's press (launcher-§6) and any other site…'.
   - **The launcher while disabled.** New bullet after the 'A launcher click MUST NOT write SavedVariables' bullet (:257): 'A key press is a feature, not setup. The Show window binding (launcher-§6) calls the toggle's handler, so while stood down it toggles nothing and writes nothing, and it answers as the `toggle` verb answers. A grayed menu entry can show its state; a key cannot, so a press that is silent where the verb would print is a finding.'
   - **Step 8 (:323)** is renamed **'The launcher and the key binding'**, and this is appended: 'Where the addon ships launcher-§6's binding, invoke the bound button's OnClick while disabled. Assert zero SavedVariables writes and zero frame shows, plus, where the addon implements §2's refusal SHOULD, exactly one line matching *The refusal line*. Then write `enabled = true`, take the `perf` hold alone and invoke it again. Assert no toggle and no match on *The refusal line*, plus, where the SHOULD is implemented, exactly one `Not available during a performance capture.` line.'

4. **standards/standards/anti-patterns.md.** New **#96** after #95 (:124), using design-std A6's list with the press bullet worded: 'a press that toggles or writes while stood down, answers differently from the `toggle` verb, or prints the disabled line under the `perf` hold alone'. Cite (`launcher-§6`, `layout-§1`, `slash-commands-§7`).

5. **standards/ADDONS.md.** After the paragraph at :34, add design-std A14's sentence: 'Show window also means the addon owes launcher-§6's key binding … No new column.'

6. **standards/STANDARDS.md**
   - Blurbs: launcher (:62), append the A15 clause; slash-commands, add 'a key binding's press refuses as the toggle does'; layout (:56), add '`Bindings.xml` owed by every Show window addon'; anti-patterns (:80) → `(#1–#96)`.
   - Changelog: insert ruling '**launcher-§6 (MUST).** …', A15's ruling (1) restated with correction (ii) and no addon count.

7. **standards/EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md:23.** Append the A16 clause ('…a Show window key binding on the same toggle handler, refusing as the toggle does (launcher-§6)').

8. **standards/NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md**
   - :108, the tree comment as in layout.
   - Item 18a (:1561): add the binding.
   - Checklist: add '- [ ] Show window key binding (launcher-§6) if the addon has a primary window'.
   - The launcher snippet section gains a Bindings.xml line plus a button snippet. Model it on QuickComms settings/SlashVerbs.lua:85-92 (V.TOGGLE_BUTTON, RegisterForClicks('AnyDown'), rawset of BINDING_NAME_) and Bindings.xml's last Binding. Route the click through the toggle handler and the hold-aware refusal helper, with no `default`. Do NOT copy QuickComms settings/SlashVerbs.lua:71 (`if NS.IsStoodDown() then return NS.Print(…DisabledLine()) end`): it is the perf-hold defect the QC item fixes in this run.

9. **NEW_ADDON.md.** The launcher step (:217-244) adds 'and, where the addon has a primary window, the Show window key binding (launcher-§6): a root Bindings.xml CLICK line and the button, from the context pack'.

10. **AUDIT.md**
    - :281: '(a `CLICK` binding, on a secure or a plain named button, carries none)'.
    - In the launcher check (:575-635), the new sub-bullet '**The Show window key binding** (`launcher-§6`, new in v2.86.0)' with design-std A19's five checks. Check 4 reads 'the press reaches the toggle's handler and refuses as the `toggle` verb does (read the handler or the helper)'.
    - :683 census: add 'the key binding: a press that toggles, writes, or answers differently from the toggle verb while stood down'.
    - :708 step 8: add the binding press.

The whole change is one commit, because check-standard's citations check needs every `launcher-§6` to resolve to the new `### 6.` heading in the same tree.

Commit: `WS-02: launcher-§6 the Show window key binding (MUST), anti-pattern #96 (LibKa0s#58)`.

Verify:
```
cd ../WowAddonStandards
bash scripts/check-standard.sh      # exit 0; anti-patterns '#1–#96 contiguous, index agrees'; citations resolve
grep -n '^### 6\. The Show window key binding' standards/standards/launcher.md
grep -c 'launcher-§6' standards/standards/*.md AUDIT.md NEW_ADDON.md standards/NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md
grep -n 'six addons\|Bank Ledger, Drop Watcher' standards/standards/launcher.md   # nothing (no enumeration)
grep -n 'default=' standards/NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md | grep -i binding   # nothing
for f in $(git diff --name-only HEAD~1); do tr -dc '\r' < $f | wc -c; done
git log -1 --format=%s | grep -q '^WS-02: '
```

items.title: preview-mode: the explicit test mode says so on the display (MUST); standalone-windows: Widgets.TestStrip SHOULD for a filter-bar window; anti-pattern #97
items.spec:
Implements design-std A4's marker bullet, A5 and #97. OWNER_SCOPE D and F bind over them. Depends on the LibKa0s item that ships W.TestStrip in Widgets minor 13 (one minor carries SearchBox and TestStrip; Widgets.lua:36 is MINOR 12 today), because the text cites its published surface. Read that item's docs/api entry for the exact names before writing.

Corrections to the design:
- (i) The marker rule covers the **explicit Test mode only**. Drop design-std A4's sentence making an unlocked display's drag handle 'the marker'. Where unlocking is the preview (preview-mode's exception, preview-mode.md:10), this rule does not apply.
- (ii) Content that names the test counts as the marker. The example is a group popup whose placeholder content reads 'Test Group — …'. Describe it; do not name the addon.
- (iii) Replace 'a collapsed title bar' with the carve-out from OWNER_SCOPE D. A display minimized with its header hidden shows no placeholder data, so it owes no marker in that state. The rule binds every layout in which placeholder data is visible.
- (iv) TestStrip's public surface is the constructor, `HEIGHT` and `strip.text` (no RESERVE). Its art is **host-passed**, a resolved path the host declares like any other icon. It has no library tooltip, so a tooltip is the host's choice. Write no wording that says the library draws `info` or owns a tooltip.

End state:

1. **standards/standards/preview-mode.md.** The file is unnumbered, so add no `### N.` heading. After the 'MUST ship a test mode' bullet (:10), add the bullet '**A test mode MUST say so on the display (v2.86.0).**':
   - While the explicit test mode is on, every display drawing placeholder data carries a visible **text** marker. The marker is readable without hovering, is localized (localization), and is visible in every layout in which the placeholder data is visible, a hidden header and a compact layout included.
   - The carve-out from (iii).
   - The measured failure, described: a meter window's test text rode its header and vanished with it while the sample bars stayed.
   - The marker's form is the addon's: a title badge, inline title text, or a strip. For a standalone window with a filter bar, standalone-windows names the recommended form.
   - Not markers: the launcher tooltip's 'Test mode: On', the Master-controls checkbox, and placeholder data that merely looks plausible. Placeholder content whose visible text names the test is a marker (ii).
   - The exception scope from (i).
   - Missing, hover-only or layout-hidden markers are #97.

2. **standards/standards/standalone-windows.md.** After the 'A wide action button keeps its label…' bullet (:40), add the A5 SHOULD reworded per (iv). A standalone window whose body sits under a filter bar SHOULD satisfy preview-mode's marker rule with LibKa0s-Widgets-1.0's `TestStrip` (Widgets minor 13, LibKa0s v1.75.0). The strip:
   - spans the window's full width between the filter bar and the body;
   - carries a mark the host passes (declared on its `LibKa0s icons:` line, library-stack-§7) and one localized line saying what test mode shows and what ends it;
   - pushes the body down by the strip's published height plus the host's gaps while it shows.
   The host owns the text, any tooltip, the placement, a two-line compact variant and when it shows. A window with no filter bar keeps whatever marker satisfies preview-mode and MAY use the strip too, for example a window whose header, and the marker in it, can be hidden. Once an addon carries v1.75.0, a host-built copy of the strip is #47. No list of adopters in the body.

3. **standards/standards/anti-patterns.md.** New **#97** after #96, from design-std A6, citing (`preview-mode`, `standalone-windows`). Its 'unmarked simulation session' bullet is deferred to WS-07. Its 'marker a layout option hides' bullet describes the header-off case.

4. **standards/STANDARDS.md**
   - The preview-mode blurb becomes 'placeholder-data preview/test mode for positionable displays; an explicit test mode says so on the display, in every layout where its sample data shows'. WS-07 extends it.
   - The standalone-windows blurb gets '; and `Widgets.TestStrip` as the test-mode marker of a window with a filter bar'.
   - Anti-patterns → `(#1–#97)`.
   - Changelog: insert the ruling '**preview-mode (MUST) and standalone-windows (SHOULD).** …'.

5. **standards/EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md.** In the options-ui/preview item, add 'an explicit test mode says so on the display, in every layout (preview-mode, #97)'.

6. **standards/NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md**
   - Item 18 (:1560): add the marker rule.
   - Checklist :1680: extend it with 'with a visible, localized test marker in every layout where the sample data shows'.

7. **AUDIT.md:884** (test-mode check): add design-std A19's 'Then check the marker' paragraph, minus its unlock-preview sentence. Add 'an addon whose test mode is the unlocked view owes no marker under this rule'. A filter-bar window not using TestStrip on v1.75.0+ is a SHOULD finding. Behavior is confirmed only by the owner's in-client smoke.

Commit: `WS-03: preview-mode test-mode marker (MUST), standalone-windows TestStrip (SHOULD), anti-pattern #97 (LibKa0s#48)`.

Verify:
```
cd ../WowAddonStandards
bash scripts/check-standard.sh                 # exit 0; '#1–#97'
grep -c '^### [0-9]' standards/standards/preview-mode.md standards/standards/standalone-windows.md   # 0 and 0
grep -n 'drag handle' standards/standards/preview-mode.md   # no marker sentence about the unlock preview
grep -n 'RESERVE' -r standards AUDIT.md        # nothing
for f in $(git diff --name-only HEAD~1); do tr -dc '\r' < $f | wc -c; done
git log -1 --format=%s | grep -q '^WS-03: '
```

items.title: documentation-§1 item 12: Game-icons credit MUST and MIT-set credit SHOULD for the LibKa0s icon sets an addon ships
issue_refs: design-std A7, A11.6 (attribution sentence), A15, A17, A18, A19
items.spec:
Implements design-std A7 as written. Owner decision (#55): the rule lives in the standard, credits go into each addon's README at its re-vendor, and there is no in-game helper.

End state:

1. **standards/standards/documentation.md**
   - **Item 12 (:95).** Replace the opening clause with design-std A7's text:
     - MAY for discretionary external credit, with two exceptions for the LibKa0s icon sets the addon ships after the prune, as its `LibKa0s icons:` line decides (library-stack-§7, *The icon subset*).
     - **MUST** where any `gi:` icon ships (`all` included). Credit Game-icons.net with: the set name; CC BY 3.0; a link to https://game-icons.net; the authors of the shipped marks (`Media.IconAuthor(name)` per icon, or the shipped game-icons/AUTHORS.txt in full for `all`); and a statement that the marks were modified (rasterized, background removed, recolored).
     - **SHOULD** for each shipped MIT set: Open Iconic (unprefixed names, Waybury) and Phosphor (`ph:`, Phosphor Icons), each with author, license and link.
     - Credit goes by set, only for the sets that ship, and never to LibKa0s as a library (the inventory ban, anti-pattern #58, unchanged).
     - A set that stops shipping loses its credit line in the commit that prunes it.
     - The rest of item 12 is unchanged (last section, no library list).
   - **:117.** Replace with A7's line: Credits is MAY, except item 12 makes it MUST where a `gi:` icon ships and SHOULD where an MIT set ships.
   - **:109-113**, the inventory-ban passage: add a clause that icon-set credit under item 12 is external credit and survives the ban.

2. **standards/standards/library-stack.md**, the bullet *Attribution travels with its set (MUST)* (:188-192). Append: 'The README half, crediting the sets that ship, is documentation-§1 item 12: a MUST for Game-icons, a SHOULD for the MIT sets.'

3. **standards/STANDARDS.md**
   - The documentation blurb: add 'the README credits the LibKa0s icon sets it ships, MUST for Game-icons (CC BY 3.0), SHOULD for the MIT sets'.
   - Changelog: insert the ruling '**documentation-§1 item 12.** …'.

4. **NEW_ADDON.md:310.** Becomes '`## Credits` carries only external credit, and **must** credit Game-icons (and **should** credit each MIT icon set) that the addon's `LibKa0s icons:` line ships (documentation-§1 item 12)'.

5. **standards/NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md.** Add the checklist line '- [ ] `## Credits` names each LibKa0s icon set shipped (documentation-§1 item 12)'. The scaffold's `close, copy, clear` are Open Iconic, so the README template gains an Open Iconic credit line (SHOULD).

6. **AUDIT.md:88-96** (README check). Add: where the `LibKa0s icons:` line ships a `gi:` icon, a `## Credits` crediting Game-icons per item 12 (missing is a MUST finding); each shipped MIT set named (missing is a SHOULD finding); no credit line for a set the prune removed.

Commit: `WS-04: documentation-§1 item 12 icon-set credits (LibKa0s#55)`.

Verify:
```
cd ../WowAddonStandards
bash scripts/check-standard.sh
grep -n 'game-icons.net' standards/standards/documentation.md AUDIT.md NEW_ADDON.md
grep -n 'is optional and carries \*\*only external' NEW_ADDON.md   # nothing
for f in $(git diff --name-only HEAD~1); do tr -dc '\r' < $f | wc -c; done
git log -1 --format=%s | grep -q '^WS-04: '
```

items.title: automated-tests-§3: a crashed or bounded lizard run is not a complexity pass (clarification); the hazard row split by line shape; anti-pattern #92; AUTOMATED_TESTS.md and playbook ripple
items.spec:
Implements design-std A8, the #92 edit in A6, and A20. OWNER_SCOPE F binds: this is a **clarification**. The release gate stays 'complexity pass', and `crashedFiles` appears only as a parenthetical, never as a new gate term.

Depends on the LibKa0s kit revision 41 item. Copy the exact names from that item's docs/api/testkit/version-41-docs.md and CHANGELOG: the manifest field `suites.complexity.crashedFiles`, the watch-list line 'Not measured — lizard raised', `n/a (lizard raised)`, status `fail`, CCN figures zeroed, parity skipped, a per-file retry naming the file, stderr out of the parse, `fld` numeric.

This item's text closes WowAddonStandards#8, which is open, untriaged, severity:low, titled 'automated-tests hazard table: the for-in function-literal row says silent drop; at file scope lizard 1.24.0 crashes'. WS-12 does the GitHub close. The corrected fact: the axis is the line's **shape**, not its scope.

End state:

1. **standards/standards/automated-tests.md**
   - **Hazard table (:149-155).** Replace the single row with design-std A8's two rows:
     - A function literal in a for/while header table, on one line or positional: not listed. Inside a function its body folds into the enclosing CCN.
     - A **keyed** function literal in a multi-line for/while header table constructor: lizard 1.24.0 raises TypeError and measures nothing after it, at file scope or inside a function.
     Add the remedy paragraph under the table. Hoist the table to a named local. The kit's sanitizer does not rewrite the shape, because renaming the header keyword drops the loop's decision point and under-counts the enclosing function. Keep the measured instance, PGFE RegionTags.lua, hoisted in 10350bc.
   - **After the parity bullet,** a clarification bullet:
     - A run in which lizard raised, or which the kit's bound stopped, is complexity **not passing**.
     - The blind/crashed distinction.
     - The `@` rows that stream before the traceback are partial and in walk order, not a measurement.
     - What the runner does from kit revision 41 (LibKa0s v1.75.0), steps 1-5 as in A8: (1) stderr out of the parse and the exact footer shape only; (2) status `fail`; (3) every CCN figure 0 in manifest.json, printed `n/a (lizard raised)`; (4) parity skipped; (5) a per-file retry that names the files, with the count recorded as the field (`suites.complexity.crashedFiles`, 0 on a measured run, absent before kit 41).
     - A bounded stop is the same `fail`, named as the bound, with no retry.
     - An exit of 1 with a valid footer and empty stderr is not a crash.

items.spec:
Implements design-std A4's simulator subsection and A13.

Depends on the LibKa0s item that lands Sim-1.0's session, seam and refusal, so the contract wording matches the shipped API: `Sim:NewSeam(compat, opts)`, `Sim:New(d)`, `seam:Unwrapped()`, the session-only panel position, and the refusals the library computes. Read LibKa0s docs/api for Sim before writing.

OWNER_SCOPE F and C bind:
- MAY ship. If one is shipped, it MUST be built on Sim-1.0, for a simulator first shipped on LibKa0s v1.75.0 or later.
- Adoption is otherwise required of none (WS-06's paragraph). A simulator a host wrote before v1.75.0 is not #47 until the host adopts.
- Name no addon in the section body. Drop design-std's 'Drop Watcher's /dw sim is the reference' and the list of shipping addons. A described reference implementation is allowed (STANDARDS.md:43).

End state:

1. **standards/standards/preview-mode.md.** Append the unnumbered `### The in-game simulator (MAY)`. No `### N.`: the file is in CLAUDE.md's list of eleven.
   - What it is: a session that plays scripted events through the addon's real engine.
   - An addon that ships one, first shipped on LibKa0s v1.75.0 or later, MUST build it on `LibKa0s-Sim-1.0` (library-stack-§7).
   - It MUST route every client read the simulation answers through its `NS.Compat` table, which is what the seam wraps. The seam is installed right after the compat family loads; a read cached in a local before then answers live data.
   - It MUST refuse to start: while stood down, with the line by hold (slash-commands-§7, the SHOULD as it stands); while test mode is on; and in combat, in an instance or in a group. The major computes the last three, and the host supplies the first two.
   - It MUST NOT send anything (every outward member is in the host's guarded set), act on a real player, or write SavedVariables from a simulated event. The panel position is session-only. A session log kept in memory and dropped at stop is not SavedVariables.
   - It MUST leave the addon exactly as it was at stop, with every module that the session touched registering its cleanup.
   - It MUST mark the session on the display, per the marker bullet. The major's step panel on screen satisfies this.
   - Slash-only (`/<slash> sim …`): no launcher entry and no key binding. A launcher entry would trigger launcher-§6.
   - Host members never hang on the library instance (OWNER_SCOPE C.4), and the host suite asserts `Unwrapped()` is empty (C.8).
   - 'These are the host's contract. The library guarantees only the refusal it computes and never advertises the rest as enforced (LibKa0s#54).'

2. **standards/standards/compat.md**, after *The applicability condition* (:17). Add A13's sentence: an addon that ships an in-game simulator routes through its compat family every client read the simulation answers, deprecated or not. Such a read is a family member, and the condition never exempts it.

items.title: Close WowAddonStandards#8 (state:done) with the corrected hazard facts, after the owner's merge go-ahead
items.spec:
A GitHub-only action with no commit. It is recorded in the bundle's exceptions.tsv with a proof command, following the 2026-10-07 precedent (LK-11, PM-10 rows).

Precondition: the owner has approved the merge, and the v2.86.0 branch is merged into master `--no-ff` and pushed through /dev-copilot:finalize. The comment cites that merge SHA, and the WS-05 commit SHA too.

Verified 2026-10-22: #8 exists, is OPEN, and is labeled bug, documentation, state:untriaged and severity:low. Its title: 'automated-tests hazard table: the for-in function-literal row says silent drop; at file scope lizard 1.24.0 crashes'.

Action (space GitHub writes; the throttle memory applies):
```
gh issue comment 8 --repo tusharsaxena/WowAddonStandards --body '<comment>'
gh issue edit 8 --repo tusharsaxena/WowAddonStandards --remove-label state:untriaged --add-label state:done
gh issue close 8 --repo tusharsaxena/WowAddonStandards --reason completed
```
The comment carries four things:
- Fixed in v2.86.0 (WS-05 <sha>, merge <sha>).
- The corrected fact. The axis is the line's shape, not its scope. A single-line or positional function literal in a for/while header table is blind (not listed). A keyed function literal in a multi-line header table constructor makes lizard 1.24.0 raise, at file scope or inside a function.
- automated-tests-§3 now treats a crashed or bounded run as complexity not passing. LibKa0s kit revision 41 zeroes the figures and names the file (`crashedFiles`).
- The remedy is to hoist the table to a local (PGFE 10350bc).

Leave #10, #11 and #12 untouched.

items.title: New major LibKa0s-Glow-1.0 (Glow minor 1): the stateless LibCustomGlow-1.0 driver
items.spec: Test first. Design inputs/design-glow.md §1-§3 and §7, with OWNER_SCOPE E binding. END STATE: new LibKa0s/Glow.lua (~110 lines): floor `NEEDS_CORE = 1` (no Core member called; returns before NewLibrary when unmet); `LibStub:NewLibrary("LibKa0s-Glow-1.0", 1)`; lib.MAJOR/MINOR; `lib.MODULES.Glow = MINOR`. Exactly two members besides MAJOR/MINOR/MODULES, dot-called: `lib.Start(frame, style, knobs, key, frameLevel) -> boolean` and `lib.Stop(frame, style, key)`. No STYLES member, no ranges, no defaults, no Available(). Style vocabulary closed: 'button', 'proc', 'pixel', 'autocast'; anything else is a quiet false/no-op. LibCustomGlow-1.0 is resolved at EVERY call with `LibStub("LibCustomGlow-1.0", true)` (no memo, no load-time capture); each LCG member presence-checked (`type(fn)=='function'`). Start: nil frame, unknown style, absent LCG or missing `_Start` -> false, nothing called. knobs: a table, else a shared empty constant (no allocation); unnamed fields ignored. Color lives in `knobs.color` (passed by reference; host must not mutate it after handing it over). Mapping (design-glow §2 table): pixel -> PixelGlow_Start(frame, color, num(pixelLines), num(pixelFrequency), len(pixelLength), num(pixelThickness), num(xOffset), num(yOffset), pixelBorder ~= false, key, frameLevel); autocast -> AutoCastGlow_Start(frame, color, num(autocastParticles), num(autocastFrequency), num(autocastScale), num(xOffset), num(yOffset), key, frameLevel); button -> ButtonGlow_Start(frame, color, num(buttonFrequency), frameLevel) (no key); proc -> ProcGlow_Start(frame, a FRESH table per call {color, startAnim = procStartAnim ~= false, duration = num(procDuration), xOffset, yOffset, key, frameLevel}), never the caller's knobs and never a reused scratch. num(v) = v when a number else nil; len(v) = v when a number > 0 else nil. `pixelBorder` and `procStartAnim` coerced `~= false` (OWNER_SCOPE E). Start never stops anything first. Stop: style given -> only that style's _Stop (button: ButtonGlow_Stop(frame) with no key; others X_Stop(frame, key)); style nil -> all four in order button, pixel, autocast, proc (OWNER_SCOPE E: a nil-style Stop stops every style); unknown style string -> no-op; nil frame or absent LCG -> no-op; missing _Stop skipped. Header: why it exists (three hosts mapped the same knobs to the same positional arguments with the same two traps), the seven traps, and 'what it deliberately is not' (design-glow §7 table, each with its trigger). No new anti-pattern sentence for the fork (OWNER_SCOPE E). REGISTRATION: LibKa0s/LibKa0s.xml `<Script file="Glow.lua"/>` after Item.lua, before Media.lua; tests/majors.lua row `{ major = "LibKa0s-Glow-1.0", files = { "Glow" }, primary = "Glow" }` in the same slot (after Item); tests/run.lua lists `test_glow` (after test_item) and may publish `glow = mocks.LibStub("LibKa0s-Glow-1.0")` beside item (:49). The 14 cases of design-glow §3 (absent LCG; call-time resolution after load; pixel 11-position vector; pixelLength 0/-3/'6'/nil -> nil and 6 -> 6; booleans; numeric type guard; autocast 9 and button 4 positions; proc options not knobs, getmetatable(knobs)==nil after, fresh per call, nil knobs -> only startAnim true; nil and non-table knobs; unknown style and nil frame; missing member; Stop shapes incl. stop-all order and button keyless n==1; stateless/no gate; a lint-style assertion that Glow.lua names no LibStub(...) outside the LCG resolver and the Core probe), each with a `-- red under:` line. items.title: New major LibKa0s-Sim-1.0 (1/5): Sim.lua and the Compat answer seam, Sim:NewSeam
items.spec: Test first. Design inputs/design-sim.md §2.1-§2.2, with OWNER_SCOPE C binding over it. END STATE: new LibKa0s/Sim.lua: floor NEEDS_CORE = 1; `LibStub:NewLibrary("LibKa0s-Sim-1.0", 1)`; MAJOR/MINOR; `lib.MODULES.Sim = 1`. `function lib:NewSeam(compat, opts) -> seam`: compat (table, required, the host's own Compat table, wrapped IN PLACE, once); opts.name (string, required, for errors and debug lines); opts.pure ({[key]=true}, never wrapped); opts.guarded ({[key]=fn}, the safe answer while a session is active); opts.debug (optional fn(tag, fmt, ...), the sink Live writes a traceback to until a session binds; after binding the session's d.debug is used). Wrap rule: every member with type 'function' not in pure is replaced by a closure whose idle path is one upvalue-field test: `if state.active and (g or not state.bypass) then return answer(key, live, g, ...) end return live(...)`; answer calls `provider(fallback, ...)` with fallback = guarded[key] or live, or fallback(...) with no provider. A guarded member never reaches the client while active, including inside Live and from a provider (a provider's first argument is the guarded fn, never live); idle, guarded members call live. Seam members: `SetProvider(key, fn)` (nil removes; RAISES on a key not wrapped (pure or unknown) and RAISES when a second non-nil provider is set for a key that already has one, OWNER_SCOPE C.8), `Live(fn, ...)` (bypass=true, nesting-safe, restored on every exit; an error is re-raised with its ORIGINAL value via error(v, 0) so tables survive, after the traceback is written to the debug sink; nil holes in returns survive via select('#')), `Keys()` (sorted wrapped keys), `Unwrapped()` (sorted keys of function members of compat that are neither pure nor still the recorded wrapper: a member added after NewSeam or replaced; every host suite asserts it is empty, C.8). NOT built (C.7/C.8): no seam:IsActive, no seam:IsGuarded, no __newindex auto-wrap. The seam's active flag is driven only by a bound session (LK-13); until then it is idle. Header: why this is a library (three hosts, the same seam semantics, #54 and the owner's ruling), what it deliberately is not (C.7 cuts, C.9: restriction/chat-lockdown simulation stays host code, the library never touches SavedVariables, no behavior flags), and the payload-weight note (three file bodies, no frame/timer/event until NewSeam/New is called). REGISTRATION: LibKa0s.xml `<Script file="Sim.lua"/>` after PerfPanel.lua; tests/majors.lua row `{ major = "LibKa0s-Sim-1.0", files = { "Sim" }, primary = "Sim" }` after Perf (LK-14/LK-16 grow it). TESTS: new tests/test_sim_seam.lua (run.lua after the perf suites): every non-pure function is wrapped and Keys() is sorted; an idle call goes straight to live (and the closure adds no allocation); providers get the fallback; with a test-only active flag driven through a minimal bound session stub is NOT available yet, so active-path cases drive the seam through a file-local test hook documented as internal (`seam.__setActive`, removed or kept as a documented test seam by LK-13 when real sessions exist) OR are deferred to LK-13; SetProvider raises on a pure key, an unknown key and a second owner, and nil releases; Live restores bypass when fn raises, re-raises a table error value unchanged (rawequal), writes the traceback to opts.debug, keeps nil holes; Unwrapped lists a late-added member and a replaced member and is empty otherwise. DOCS: docs/api/Sim/version-1-docs.md (Current, the seam contract so far, 'Sessions arrive in the next commit of this release') + `lua tools/gen-api-members.lua` -> docs/api/Sim/members-1.json; docs/api/README.md version-key row (`LibKa0s-Sim-1.0 | <Sim>.<SimTimeline>.<SimPanel> | LibStub("LibKa0s-Sim-1.0").MODULES`) and a `### LibKa0s-Sim-1.0` section. CHANGELOG v1.75.0: `Sim minor 1` and a `### LibKa0s-Sim-1.0 (new major)` section opened with the seam and the payload-weight note. US English; ASCII only in LibKa0s/ (em dash excepted, test_prose). Every function CCN <= 15. Regenerate docs/test-cases.md. Commit `LK-12: LibKa0s-Sim-1.0 (Sim minor 1): the Compat answer seam (#54)`. items.title: Sim-1.0 (2/5): the session, Sim:New, Start/Stop with guarded and cleanup phases, Fire, After, listeners
items.spec: Test first. Design inputs/design-sim.md §2.3, §2.6, §5, with OWNER_SCOPE C binding. END STATE in LibKa0s/Sim.lua (stays under ~600 lines; split helpers so no function exceeds CCN 15): `function lib:New(d) -> sim`. Required fields (missing -> raise naming the field, Perf's required() style): name, seam (from NewSeam; RAISE if the seam is already bound: one seam binds one session), slash, deliver (fn(event, ...) -> n; any string legal), isStoodDown (fn, read at call time), scenarios ({names, defs = {[name] = {label, sizes?, timeline = fn(def, opts) -> steps}}}), prepare (fn(session, def, opts, ready)), play (fn(step, session) -> detail?; used by LK-14). Optional: refusal (fn(opts) -> line|nil), gate, stepDelay, verbs, why, usage, statusLine (LK-14/15), stopText ({[reason]=line}), L (STRINGS overridable via rawget, Perf's tr, Perf.lua:590-594), print, debug (tag SIM, read at call time; defaults DEFAULT_CHAT_FRAME and a no-op), panel (LK-16; panel fields allowed: title, stepLabel, stepTip, startTip, stopTip, anchorTo, check. NO button, NO tooltip, NO store: C.7 and C.11). Instance members: `Start(opts)` -> ok, line: order (1) unknown scenario -> UNKNOWN_SCENARIO plus the names, (2) ALREADY_RUNNING, (3) refusal(opts) run INSIDE seam:Live, (4) backstop isStoodDown() -> STOOD_DOWN; then session {sim=true, scenario, size, seed, startedAt=time(), events=0} (size reaches prepare only when def.sizes exists; 0 = random; seed defaults to a time-derived integer), seam active, print STARTED (neutral, no saved-data claim; each host overrides it with its own guarantee line), prepare under pcall with a `ready` closure BOUND TO THIS SESSION: a ready() from a stale session (after restart, or stop then start) is ignored, a second ready() is ignored (C.1); a prepare error becomes Stop('error'); notify listeners. `Stop(reason)` -> bool (reason defaults 'stop'): RE-ENTRANCY-SAFE: answers false once `stopping` is set (a Stop inside Fire -> deliver, inside play/listener/OnStop callbacks, or a second Stop is a no-op) and false when idle (C.1). Order, each step after 1 pcalled: (1) cancel the run and every session timer, (2) mark stopping (IsActive stays true, seam still answers, Fire and After refuse), (3) OnStopGuarded list, (4) seam off, clear session and delivering, enter cleanup phase, (5) OnStop list, (6) leave cleanup; hide the panel if isStoodDown() else repaint; notify, (7) print stopText[reason] or the library line for stop/restart/error or STOPPED_REASON, plus one debug line with event count and reason. Library-emitted reasons: stop, restart, error, standDown. `IsActive()` (no public active field), `IsDelivering()` (true only inside Fire, nesting-safe), `Session()` (host fields go on the session table, the host bag), `Fire(event, ...)` -> n (0 unless active, not stopping and not stood down; an observed stand-down while active first calls Stop('standDown'); increments events, debug line, sets delivering, pcalls deliver, restores delivering; error -> debug line, 0), `After(delay, fn)` -> handle|nil (nil when idle; fires only while the same session is live, under pcall; handle:Cancel() cancels AND forgets; all live handles cancelled at stop), `OnStopGuarded(fn)` and `OnStop(fn)` (permanent, ordered registrations), `DeliverForCleanup(event, ...)` -> n (delivers only during the OnStop phase with the seam off AND answers 0 while isStoodDown(): DW's stood-down check kept, C.3), `Status()` -> {active, scenario, size, seed, startedAt, events, ready, pos, total, playing, paused, settling}, `AddListener(fn)` (fn(sim) under pcall on start, ready, step, run, pause, stop; permanent). NO sim:Live (C.7: one Live, on the seam). Fallbacks: Sim.lua installs no-op members for every timeline, verb and panel member (RunVerb prints NO_TIMELINE and answers false, 'absent'; Steps/PanelRows answer {}), which LK-14..LK-16's attach files overwrite (Perf's no-panel pattern, Perf.lua:970-978). Host contract C.4 written into the header and doc: host members never hang on the library instance; the host keeps its own table (e.g. NS.SimHost) for Status extras, HistoryLog, MarkGUID, SetRestriction and the like, and holds the seam separately for SetProvider. STRINGS (built-in English, all overridable): STARTED, STOPPED, STOPPED_RESTART, STOPPED_ERROR, STOPPED_REASON, ALREADY_RUNNING, STOOD_DOWN, UNKNOWN_SCENARIO, NOT_RUNNING, NO_TIMELINE (plus the timeline/verb/panel keys LK-14..16 add). If LK-12 used a temporary `seam.__setActive` hook, remove it here and drive the seam's active path only through sessions. TESTS: new tests/test_sim_session.lua: required-field raises; second New on one seam raises; refusal order and refusal-inside-Live (a seam member read in refusal answers live during a session restart); stood-down backstop; Start prints and creates the session; size only with sizes; stale ready ignored after restart and after stop+start (C.1); second ready ignored; Fire 0 when idle, stood down or stopping; a stand-down self-stops; deliver errors isolated; nested Fire restores delivering; After fires only within its session, Cancel forgets, all cancelled at stop; Stop order guarded -> seam off -> cleanup, each step pcalled (a raising OnStopGuarded does not skip the rest); Stop re-entered from inside deliver, from an OnStop callback and twice in a row is a no-op answering false (C.1); DeliverForCleanup legal only in the cleanup phase and 0 while stood down (C.3); guarded members answer guarded inside Live during a session and live when idle; reason lines, stopText and STRINGS overrides via rawget (a locale table with a metatable fallback does not shadow the built-in). Move LK-12's deferred active-path seam cases here. DOCS: extend docs/api/Sim/version-1-docs.md (session contract, stop order, host bag, C.4) and regenerate members-1.json. CHANGELOG Sim section extended. Regenerate docs/test-cases.md. Commit `LK-13: Sim-1.0: the session, two-phase stop, Fire, After (#54)`. VERIFY: lua tests/run.lua (0 failed); luacheck . 0/0; `grep -n 'function lib:New\b\|function lib:New(' LibKa0s/Sim.lua`; `grep -n ':Live(' LibKa0s/Sim.lua` shows only the seam's member and refusal call sites; wc -l LibKa0s/Sim.lua < 1000.

items.title: Sim-1.0 (3/5): SimTimeline.lua, the step machine with the host gate, per-step delay and the internal RunTo
items.spec: Test first. Design inputs/design-sim.md §2.4 (step machine half), OWNER_SCOPE C binding. END STATE: new LibKa0s/SimTimeline.lua, a secondary file paired on Sim's minor: `local TIMELINE_MINOR = 1`, guard on `lib.__timelineMinor` / `lib.__timelineShellMinor == lib.MINOR`, `lib.MODULES.SimTimeline = 1`; attaches through a `lib.__AttachTimeline` handshake that Sim.lua's New calls (overwriting LK-13's fallbacks); no floor beyond Sim itself. Members on the instance: `Steps()` (the live list; {} idle), `Step()` -> step or nil, code (notRunning, building (until the bound ready()), done, settling: the gate is closed, its line or SETTLING printed, pos does not advance; on success advance pos, pcall play, stamp ranAt and detail and index (the library writes nothing else into a step), print STEP_LINE, notify; a play error counts the step as run with detail ERROR, pauses the run, prints STEP_FAILED), `Run()` -> true or false, code (notRunning, building, playing, done): clears paused, plays to the end; each tick checks the gate: closed -> re-poll after GATE_POLL = 0.25 s without advancing; open -> Step then schedule the next tick after stepDelay(step) (a number or fn(step) -> seconds, default 2, read when each timer is set; per C.11 a host passes a fixed constant, there is no schema row); at the end prints FINISHED formatted with slash and notifies; `Pause()` (notPlaying) cancels the pending tick with no orphan timer, `Resume()` (notPaused) calls Run, `Restart()` (notRunning) = Stop('restart') then Start{scenario, size} with a fresh seed, a refusal printed and answered false, 'refused'. RunTo is SIM-INTERNAL (C.7): a file-local function handed to SimPanel through the attach handshake, never an instance member: plays steps up to and including index back to back (no stepDelay), honoring the gate by polling, synchronous when the gate stays open; a step failure or a done/notRunning answer ends it; it occupies Run's `playing` slot (C.2): while a RunTo poll is pending, Run answers 'playing', Pause cancels it, Stop cancels it, a second click-ahead answers 'playing'. Session token (C.1, critique B1): Step, every Run tick and RunTo capture the session before play and bail if it changed afterwards (no ranAt/detail stamp, no STEP_LINE, no next tick). gate: optional fn(session) -> open, line?; checked before every step by Step, Run ticks and RunTo; no gate = always open (DW); LH passes its Reconciler settle (C.12). Status() gains pos, total, playing, paused, settling, ready. All timers through LK-13's session After, so they die with the session. STRINGS added: BUILDING, PLAYING, NOT_PLAYING, NOT_PAUSED, DONE, SETTLING, STEP_LINE ('Simulation step %d of %d: %s.'), STEP_FAILED, FINISHED ('Simulation finished: %s stop ends it.'), ERROR. REGISTRATION: LibKa0s.xml `<Script file="SimTimeline.lua"/>` after Sim.lua; tests/majors.lua Sim row files {Sim, SimTimeline} and paired `{ file = "SimTimeline", minorField = "__timelineMinor", probeField = "__timelineShellMinor" }`. Sim key 1 -> 1.1: LK-02's unreleased-key rule (git mv docs/api/Sim/version-1-docs.md and members-1.json to the 1.1 names, rewrite header and 'What changed', regenerate, README row). TESTS: new tests/test_sim_timeline.lua using the kit clock: building until ready(), a second ready ignored, done at the end; gate settling line without advancing; Run with a delay per step through fn(step) and with a constant; the gate poll at 0.25 s; Pause leaves no orphan timer, Resume continues, Restart uses a fresh seed and re-runs prepare; RunTo synchronous with an open gate, waiting while closed; Run during a pending RunTo poll answers playing, Pause cancels the poll, Stop cancels it (C.2); a play error pauses and prints STEP_FAILED; a Stop inside play leaves no stamp, no STEP_LINE and no next tick (token); a restart during an async prepare: the old ready() is ignored (C.1); listeners fire on start, ready, step, run, pause, stop; Status fields. RunTo is reached through the attach handshake's documented internal table, not an instance member (assert `sim.RunTo == nil`). CHANGELOG `SimTimeline minor 1`. Regenerate docs/test-cases.md. Commit `LK-14: Sim-1.0: SimTimeline.lua, the gated step machine (#54)`. items.title: Sim-1.0 (4/5): the verbs, sim:RunVerb with the generic grammar, host verbs, WHY lines, status and usage
items.spec: Test first. Design inputs/design-sim.md §2.4 (verbs half), with OWNER_SCOPE C.7 (no `help` verb). END STATE in LibKa0s/SimTimeline.lua (no minor change: unreleased): `sim:RunVerb(line) -> ok, code`, printing every result through d.print. Generic grammar: empty line -> status line plus usage, and opens the panel (a no-op until LK-16); `start <name> [size]` -> Start; `run` / `step` / `pause` / `resume` / `restart` / `stop` -> the control of the same name; `status` -> status line; `panel` -> TogglePanel. NO `help` verb (C.7): anything unknown, including 'help', prints usage. After the generic verbs, d.verbs ({[verb] = {parse = fn(words) -> cmd|nil, run = fn(cmd, sim) -> ok, code, free = bool?}}) are tried; a host verb needs an active session unless free. Free verbs: status, start, panel and the empty line; every other verb (the host's too unless free) prints NOT_RUNNING when idle. A failure code prints its WHY line from the library's codes (notRunning, building, playing, done, settling, notPlaying, notPaused) plus d.why; `refused` stays silent (its line already printed). Status line: STATUS_IDLE / STATUS_RUNNING with scenario, size, seed, pos/total, playing/paused/settling, plus d.statusLine(status, session) appended (line or list). Usage: USAGE_* lines formatted with d.slash, plus d.usage lines. The click path is the typed path: LK-16's panel calls RunVerb (or the internal RunTo, which prints the same per-step lines). Host wiring (documented, not enforced): one Slash-1.0 feature-verb row `{"sim", desc, function(rest) NS.Sim:RunVerb(rest) end}`, refused while the addon is disabled; slash-only, no launcher entry and no key binding (C.11). STRINGS added: STATUS_IDLE, STATUS_RUNNING, USAGE_* (one per generic verb), WHY_* as needed. TESTS: new tests/test_sim_verbs.lua: every generic verb dispatches to its control and prints exactly the control's lines; start with and without size, unknown scenario line; 'help' and 'bogus' print usage (red under: a help verb); free verbs work idle, others print NOT_RUNNING idle; host verbs parse/run, a free host verb runs idle, a host failure code prints d.why's line; refused is silent; status line merges d.statusLine (string and list forms); usage appends d.usage and formats slash; empty line prints status and usage. Docs: extend docs/api/Sim/version-1.1-docs.md (verbs, grammar, the one slash row) and regenerate members-1.1.json if the lib-level surface moved. CHANGELOG Sim section extended. Regenerate docs/test-cases.md. Commit `LK-15: Sim-1.0: RunVerb, the generic grammar and host verbs (#54)`. items.title: Sim-1.0 (5/5): SimPanel.lua, the docked step panel, picker and controls, session-only position
items.spec: Test first. Design inputs/design-sim.md §2.5, with OWNER_SCOPE C binding and LK-11's outcome deciding the renderer. END STATE: new LibKa0s/SimPanel.lua paired on Sim's minor: `local SIM_PANEL_MINOR = 1`, guard on `lib.__panelMinor` / `lib.__panelShellMinor == lib.MINOR`, `lib.MODULES.SimPanel = 1`, attached through `lib.__AttachPanel`-style handshake from New (overwriting LK-13's no-op panel fallbacks). Attach-file floor (so a headless Sim, seam+session+timeline, is never lost to a missing panel): OUTCOME A: Widgets with `MODULES.WidgetsStepPanel >= 1` (renders through W.StepPanel); OUTCOME B: Core >= 9 and Widgets present (W.Dropdown for the picker), and the renderer is LK-10's widget code carried as a FILE-LOCAL section of SimPanel.lua (library-internal, no public contract), with a header line noting the deliberate duplication with PerfPanel.lua, reachable by tests only through a documented internal test seam `lib.__StepPanel` (narrowed `__` clause). Rows: Start, one row per step, Stop, addressed by INDEX. States: timeline row before pos done (not actionable), at pos while playing or settling busy, at pos+1 ready (actionable), further ahead locked AND actionable (click-ahead via the internal RunTo), any timeline row while idle or before ready locked not actionable; Start row ready when idle (actionable), busy until ready, then done; Stop row cancel while running (actionable only then). No new state (D8). Command column `slash..' start '..name[..' '..size]`, `slash..' step'`, `slash..' stop'`. Tips: d.panel.stepTip/startTip/stopTip; a done row adds RAN_AGO. Footer: idle = the picker (scenario W.Dropdown from names/label; size W.Dropdown only when the picked def has sizes, with RANDOM = 0; Start); running = controls (Run all, Pause/Resume swapping, Restart, Stop) using the library's default minimal Core-skinned button (no d.panel.button, C.7) and GameTooltip (no d.panel.tooltip, C.7). Click: re-compose from the live model and re-check the clicked index (a stale row never acts); every action goes through RunVerb or the internal RunTo (click path = typed path). Preview while idle: the picked scenario's timeline(def, opts) at pos 0, all rows locked. Refresh on every listener notification; ShowPanel answers false and does nothing while stood down; hidden on a stand-down stop. Height bounds re-pinned on row-count change (inherited from StepPanel, C.5). Placement (C.7: no StepPanel place/onDragStop, so SimPanel positions the frame itself and hooks OnDragStop with HookScript): a point dragged THIS SESSION wins, held in instance memory only (C.11: session-only, nothing written to SavedVariables; no d.panel.store); else dock right of d.panel.anchorTo(), or left if no room, or float CENTER +420 when neither fits, DOCK_GAP = 8; it redocks on the next Show with no dragged point; ResetPanelPosition() forgets the point. Members: ShowPanel, HidePanel, TogglePanel, IsPanelShown, RefreshPanel, ResetPanelPosition, PanelRows() (pure composed list {key, index, label, command, state, actionable, tip}, published so host suites assert rows without __ fields). d.panel fields: title (default name..' - Simulation'), stepLabel(step, i, steps) (default step.label or step.kind), stepTip, startTip, stopTip, anchorTo, check (HOST-PASSED done-mark texture, e.g. the host's NS.Icon('confirm'); not library-drawn, so the closed library-drawn set does not grow). STRINGS added: PANEL_START, PANEL_STOP, RUN_ALL, PAUSE, RESUME, RESTART, STOP, RANDOM, RAN_AGO. REGISTRATION: LibKa0s.xml `<Script file="SimPanel.lua"/>` after SimTimeline.lua; tests/majors.lua Sim row files {Sim, SimTimeline, SimPanel} and paired `{ file = "SimPanel", minorField = "__panelMinor", probeField = "__panelShellMinor" }`. items.title: Sim-1.0 contract tests: two-copy pairing isolation, the reference degradation stub with parity, and a DW-shaped mini host end to end
items.spec: Tests only (no payload change unless a test exposes a defect, which is then fixed in this commit with its case).    (e) Show the proposed line with file:line evidence per name and confirm it with the user before the copy. In a cross-repo run whose bundle pre-decides the line (items.tsv / the item spec), record it as decided and do not re-ask. State that hand lists have drifted before (KickCD tests/test_mediasetup.lua:28, WhatGroup :19) and that the owner's in-client smoke is the backstop: a pruned icon still resolves to a path and draws blank, and the gate cannot see a name the host forgot.
6. NEW `### 3j. Tests that assume the whole icon folder (a blocker class)`. Run `grep -rn "media/icons\|lib.ICONS\|\.ICONS)" <Addon>/tests --include='*.lua' | grep -v '/_kit/'`. A suite that opens a file for every catalog name goes red after the prune (AbsorbTracker tests/test_mediasetup.lua:111-121). Fix both in Step 4's commit: delete the whole-catalog loop, because the kit gate already enforces declared == shipped, and narrow file assertions to declared names. Never write a second declaration parser in the addon.

   cp -r <scratch>/LibKa0s/. <Addon>/libs/LibKa0s/ ; cp -r <scratch>/testkit/. <Addon>/tests/_kit/ ; then both diffs in both directions, which MUST be content-empty against the WHOLE copy, BEFORE the prune ; then roll the provenance line AND write or keep the `LibKa0s icons:` line under it ; then `lua <scratch>/tools/prune-icons.lua <Addon>`.    'The provenance line' (:304-312) gains: 'and the declaration under it'. Write or keep `LibKa0s icons: …` as the next non-blank line. Split a run-on provenance sentence (3i b). From v1.75.0 every consumer declares; the no-line transition state ends at its re-vendor (library-stack-§7).

     - each shipped MIT set: SHOULD.
     - remove the credit line of a set the prune removed.
     - credit sets, never 'LibKa0s' (anti-pattern #58).
     - `## Credits` stays the last section.
   Announce it, and run the de-AI pass on the edited README lines (documentation-§1). This is the one README edit beyond removing a superseded provenance line.
   NEW paragraph, 'Dead stub mirrors': a library-absent stub that mirrors a `__` member the tag removed is dead. At v1.75.0 that is `__releaseChrome`, in the addons' settings/OptionsSetup.lua; grep `grep -rn '__releaseChrome' <Addon> --include='*.lua' --exclude-dir=libs --exclude-dir=_kit`. Remove it, and any test asserting it, in the same commit (library-stack-§7 narrowed `__` clause; KickCD M4-09 precedent).
   Commit paragraph (:324) now lists: both payloads after the prune, both CLAUDE.md lines, any provenance split, the 3g and 3j blockers, the stub mirrors and the credits, in ONE commit, because the consumer's test_vendor_sync fails a split.
8. NEW `### A tag that moved before it was pushed (a refresh)`, at the end of Step 4. The case: the provenance tag equals the newest tag, the payload diffs are not clean, and `git -C ../LibKa0s ls-remote --tags origin <tag>` prints nothing (a local-only tag that was moved on a run branch; OWNER_SCOPE B, the RV2 items). That is a refresh, not a 3a disagreement.

   - New paragraph after :73. A crashed run already fails the Complexity row on status. On that run the CCN row and the Sighted row both read NOT EVALUATED, never PASS: the warnings 0 and blindFiles 0 are zeroed or skipped, not measured. The CCN figures are zeroed in the manifest and n/a in RESULTS.md, and any `@` rows before the traceback in complexity.txt are partial, never a measurement. ANALYSIS.md must not compare them with earlier runs. Absent field = kit < 41, where a crash read as blind in every file.'

items.spec:
Follow the installed /dev-copilot:wow-revendor-libka0s at the dev-copilot 2.4.0 procedure (DC-01/DC-04), mechanically (no interview and no issue filing). AbsorbTracker adopts nothing new in this run: OWNER_SCOPE names it as an adopter of none of SearchBox, TestStrip, Glow-1.0, Sim-1.0, BonusIDsFromLink or the launcher-section-6 binding. The survey confirms it has no Show-window toggle and no explicit test mode, because its unlocked bar is the preview, which WS-03 carves out. So this is the ONLY item for this repo. Default branch master; run branch feat/2026-10-22-libka0s-issues-45-58. Base: CLAUDE.md:43 reads `Bundles [LibKa0s](https://github.com/tusharsaxena/LibKa0s) v1.71.0 (MIT).`, and the payload matches the v1.71.0 tag byte for byte, at kit 38. v1.72.0..v1.74.0 were never vendored here, so they ride in this delta and no span bundle is owed.

(1) PAYLOAD. Export the LOCAL tag with `git -C ../LibKa0s archive v1.75.0 LibKa0s testkit | tar -x -C <scratch>`, never the working tree. Copy LibKa0s/ whole into libs/LibKa0s/ (it gains OptionsDrawer.lua, MediaIcons.lua, Glow.lua, the Sim files and WidgetsStepPanel.lua if LK-11 made it public, the 5,836-icon media/icons with phosphor/ and game-icons/, and LibKa0s.xml) and testkit/ whole into tests/_kit/ (it gains latch.lua). Delete only the 'Only in' files. Kit.VERSION in tests/_kit/framework.lua becomes 41. Run both diffs (--strip-trailing-cr content, and bytes) BEFORE the prune; both must be empty.

(2) CLAUDE.md, in the same commit. Roll line 43 to `Bundles [LibKa0s](https://github.com/tusharsaxena/LibKa0s) v1.75.0 (MIT).`. Line 43 is the file's last line, so there is no provenance paragraph to split. Add the declaration as the NEXT NON-BLANK line, exactly:
`LibKa0s icons: clear, close, copy, help.`
The names are alphabetical (vendor_sync sorts them; testkit/vendor_sync.lua:244). Every name derives from a real draw site:
- help: host seam NS.Icon (core/MediaSetup.lua:120) reached from modules/Bar.lua:133 (`helpIcon = NS.Icon("help")`, the DragHandle ? mark).
- close: host, modules/Bar.lua:172 (`closeIcon = NS.Icon("close")`, the DragHandle X). Also library-drawn by Core.MakeCloseButton (LibKa0s Core.lua:242) for the DebugLog console and its Widgets Copy window, because core/DebugLogSetup.lua:135 passes addonName, and for PerfPanel's close (PerfPanel.lua:210) through core/PerfSetup.lua:45 `addonName = addonName`.
- clear, copy: library-drawn, the DebugLog console title-bar buttons (LibKa0s DebugLog.lua:292-293), wired by core/DebugLogSetup.lua.
- NOT info: the addon has no Options id list. `grep -n IdList settings modules core` finds only the inert degradation stub at settings/OptionsSetup.lua:311, and the descriptor's addonName at settings/OptionsSetup.lua:80-82 is latent. The addon hosts no W.TestStrip either. All four names are Open Iconic (unprefixed), so only the Open Iconic set and LICENSE-open-iconic.txt ship.

(3) PRUNE. From ../LibKa0s at the tag, run `lua tools/prune-icons.lua ../AbsorbTracker`. Afterwards libs/LibKa0s/media/icons/ holds exactly clear.tga, close.tga, copy.tga, help.tga and LICENSE-open-iconic.txt, with no phosphor/ or game-icons/ directory (anything outside a known set ships unpruned per vendor_sync iconCatalog). media/fonts and media/textures are untouched.

(4) ADOPTION BLOCKERS, fixed in the copy commit:
(a) Options parity (v1.73.0 O.Drawer). tests/test_surface_parity.lua:98-169 pins the Options stub with assertSurfaceParity('LibKa0s-Options-1.0', {exemptions}). Follow this file's own rule, that a member with no caller is exempt rather than stubbed (the RefreshPanel entry at :126-131; `grep -rn Drawer core modules settings` is empty). Add "Drawer" to the exemption list with a comment naming OptionsDrawer minor 1, LibKa0s v1.73.0, its single consumer QuickComms, and the grep. settings/OptionsSetup.lua is unchanged unless the gate shows the degraded build reaching Drawer.
(b) Kit 39 __fireUnconditional. The addon's only use is tests/test_disabled.lua:205, a falsification probe on the unregistered per-unit frame that expects `reached == 1`. Kit 39 now also reaches method-name and function handlers after unregister. Run the case. If `reached`, the SV-write, print or shown-frame assertions move, the fix goes in the addon's stand-down guard (core/AbsorbTracker.lua SyncUnitEventFrames or the handler), never in a weakened assertion. If it stays green, record it as 'no change' in 01_DELTA 3g.
(c) Whole-catalog icon tests, rewritten to the declaration:
- tests/test_mediasetup.lua:110-125, 'every name the library ships has a file in the vendored copy', iterates lib.ICONS and goes red after the prune. Rewrite it as 'MediaSetup: every icon CLAUDE.md declares has a file in the vendored copy'. It reads the declaration through `dofile("tests/_kit/vendor_sync.lua").iconDeclaration(<CLAUDE.md text>)`, asserts mode == 'list', and checks that each name's libs/LibKa0s/media/icons/<name>.tga exists and is non-empty. items.title: Sim host-contract refactor (no library yet): deliver beside the live dispatcher honouring rejectedEvents, NS.SimHost split off NS.Sim, the direct Sim.active/Sim.delivering reads become calls
items.spec:
Behaviour-neutral preparation for DW-02 (OWNER_SCOPE C.4, C.10; design-sim §6 H3, §10). DW's own simulator stays fully in charge; every existing sim suite passes with edits confined to moved call sites.

END STATE:
(1) core/DropWatcher.lua: new `function NS.DeliverEvent(event, ...)` next to DW:OnSharedFeatureEvent (:59-70) and registerFeatureEvents (:72-84). It walks NS.FEATURE_EVENTS rows in order, SKIPS an event listed in NS.rejectedEvents (core/CoreSetup.lua:17; an array, so a membership check), pcalls `NS.addon[method](NS.addon, event, ...)` per row, writes a `SIM` debug line `handler %s for %s failed: %s` through NS.SafeToString on a raise, never rethrows (the deliberate difference from the live dispatcher's rethrow-first-error, documented in the function's header), and answers the number of handlers called. modules/Sim.lua's local `deliver` (:145-157) is deleted and Sim.Fire/DeliverForCleanup call NS.DeliverEvent.
(2) modules/Sim.lua: a host table `NS.SimHost` (published at the top of the file) takes the host-only members off NS.Sim: HistoryLog (:77-80), MarkGUID/IsSimGUID (:84-95), SetRestriction/SetLockdown and the PROVIDERS table (:229-269), the host half of Status (:106-114: situation, members, restrictions, lockdown, groups, sends, handOvers; NS.SimHost.Status() answers it merged with NS.Sim.Status()), Refusal (:127-137) and OnWorldEvent (:381-389). The counts (Sim.counts, core/SimSeam.lua:42) move to NS.SimHost.counts, written by printSend/handOver (:55-69). Callers move: modules/History.lua:413/424 (`NS.SimHost.HistoryLog()`), modules/SimRoster.lua (MarkGUID x2), modules/SimEvents.lua (SetRestriction x5), modules/SimScenario.lua (SetLockdown x2, Refusal), settings/SimVerbs.lua (SetLockdown, Status), modules/Diagnostics.lua:372, modules/WindowTitleBar.lua:133.
(3) Every direct field read becomes a call: core/DropWatcher.lua:130 `NS.Sim.active` -> `NS.Sim.IsActive()`; modules/History.lua:413, :424, :535 (`H.LogFor(NS.Sim.IsActive())`); modules/LootFeed.lua:578-580 (`Sim.delivering`/`Sim.active` -> `Sim.IsDelivering()`/`Sim.IsActive()`); History.lua:636 drops its `NS.Sim.IsDelivering and` guard (the member always exists, stub included from DW-02). After this item `grep -rn 'Sim%.active\|Sim%.delivering\|Sim%.bypass' core modules settings` returns only core/SimSeam.lua and modules/Sim.lua (the owners), and core/State.lua:15-17's comment is corrected to name NS.Sim.IsActive().
(4) Tests (test-first for the one behaviour change, the rejected-event skip): tests/test_sim_core.lua gains `sim fire: an event the client rejected at registration is never delivered` (push the event into NS.rejectedEvents, Fire answers 0, the handler never ran; red under the old deliver) and `sim deliver: NS.DeliverEvent answers the handler count and isolates a raising handler` (moved from the :180-192/:289-304 assertions, which keep their wording). Every other sim suite edit is a renamed call site only (NS.Sim.HistoryLog -> NS.SimHost.HistoryLog, etc.); no assertion is weakened.
(5) Docs: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md event-wiring section names NS.DeliverEvent as the simulator's replay of FEATURE_EVENTS (skipping rejected events); docs/data-flow.md's sim section (~:300-330) the same; DropWatcher.toc's modules\\Sim.lua comment (:118-123) names NS.SimHost. docs/test-cases.md regenerated and the README.md:7 badge rolled.

items.spec:
The DropWatcher migration is the Sim-1.0 contract proof (OWNER_SCOPE C.10): DW's sim suites are PORTED to the library API, edits limited to call sites that moved, every behavioural assertion kept; an assertion is deleted from DW only where LK-17's DW-shaped mini host (or LK-12..LK-14's suites) asserts the same line in the library, and the commit body lists each such DW case -> library case. A gap in Sim-1.0 found here is NOT patched in libs/: it lands additively in LibKa0s on the run branch, the local v1.75.0 tag is moved, and DW gets an RV2 refresh item (OWNER_SCOPE B).

END STATE:
(1) core/SimSeam.lua is replaced by core/SimSetup.lua at the same TOC slot (DropWatcher.toc:63-67; comment rewritten LOAD-BEARING: `Sim:NewSeam wraps every NS.Compat member at load, straight after core\\Compat.lua, CompatWorld.lua and CompatItem.lua; never cache a Compat member in a local before it`). It resolves `LibStub('LibKa0s-Sim-1.0', true)` and publishes `NS.SimSeam = Sim:NewSeam(NS.Compat, { name = 'DropWatcher', pure = PURE, guarded = GUARDED })` with PURE (:45-48) and GUARDED (:75-79: ChatSender -> printSend, NotifyInspect/ClearInspectPlayer -> yes, InitiateTrade -> handOver) kept as host data, printSend/handOver writing NS.SimHost.counts. Library absent: an inert stub seam (`Live(fn, ...)` calls fn, SetProvider no-op, IsGuarded false, Keys/Unwrapped answer {}) and nothing is wrapped.
(2) modules/Sim.lua (TOC :124, still the first module) becomes descriptor wiring: `NS.Sim = Sim:New{ name='DropWatcher', seam=NS.SimSeam, slash=NS.SLASH..' sim', deliver=NS.DeliverEvent, isStoodDown=function() return NS.IsStoodDown() end, refusal=<DW's refusal: stood down via NS.StoodDownRefusal(), test mode, then combat/instance/group from NS.Situations.ReadInputs and NS.Restrictions.InCombat, each its existing L line>, scenarios=NS.SimScenarioDefs, prepare=function(...) return NS.SimScenario.Prepare(...) end, play=function(...) return NS.SimScenario.Play(...) end, stepDelay=function() return NS.SimScenario.StepDelay() end, stopText={ group=L[...], instance=L[...], standDown=L[...] } (STOP_TEXT :53-58), L=<an override table keyed by library STRINGS keys: STARTED -> DW's `Simulation started (%s): nothing is sent, and your saved history is not touched.` (locales/enUS.lua:183) and any other line a DW suite or SIM-n pins byte for byte>, print=NS.Print, debug=NS.Debug }`. `NS.SimScenarioDefs = { names = {}, defs = {} }` is published here and filled in place by modules/SimScenario.lua at load (it loads at :481, after the instance exists, because SimEvents and SimScenario register OnStop at load). If LK-13 snapshots or validates `scenarios` at New such that the in-place fill fails, that is a Sim gap handled per OWNER_SCOPE B. The library-absent path builds the inert stub of design-sim §7 (IsActive/IsDelivering/IsPanelShown false, Fire/DeliverForCleanup 0, After nil, Start false+line, RunVerb prints `The simulator needs LibKa0s-Sim-1.0.` and answers false,'absent', Stop false, OnStop/OnStopGuarded/AddListener/panel no-ops, Status {active=false}, Session nil, PanelRows/Steps {}). Host members stay on NS.SimHost (OWNER_SCOPE C.4): nothing is written onto the library instance.
(3) Stop wiring in today's order (Sim.lua:298-376): `NS.Sim:OnStopGuarded(function() NS.Asks.CancelQueued('simStop') end)` (the step that must run while the seam still guards the sender, :369); `NS.Sim:OnStop` registrations: the SimEvents and SimScenario cleanups (registered at their load, in TOC order, so they still precede the engine steps, as Sim.lua:341 runs them today), then liftRestrictions and ENGINE_STEPS (:311-350) in order. SimEvents' combat/bag undo uses `NS.Sim:DeliverForCleanup` (SimEvents.lua:511-515), legal only in the OnStop phase. The stand-down step (Sim.lua:401-403) becomes `NS.Sim:Stop('standDown')` and stays FIRST in NS.STAND_DOWN (H6). The auto-stop rows for GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE, PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD and ZONE_CHANGED_NEW_AREA (:391-399) stay FIRST in each fan-out; NS.SimHost.OnWorldEvent reads the world via `NS.SimSeam:Live(...)` and calls `NS.Sim:Stop(reason)`. The restriction/chat-lockdown model and its two providers stay host code (C.9) and register with `NS.SimSeam:SetProvider`.
(4) Plug-ins and call sites move to the library API (method calls): modules/SimEvents.lua (Fire x16, Session x6, SetProvider, DeliverForCleanup x2, AddCleanup -> OnStop), modules/SimWorld.lua (SetProvider x2 on NS.SimSeam, Live x3 on NS.SimSeam, Session x4, After, Fire), modules/SimPool.lua (After x2, Live), modules/SimRoster.lua (Session x2), modules/Situations.lua:180, modules/WindowFooter.lua:175, modules/WindowTitleBar.lua:343, core/DropWatcher.lua:130, modules/History.lua:413/424/535/636, modules/LootFeed.lua:578-580 (`NS.Sim:IsDelivering()`, `NS.Sim:IsActive()`, `NS.SimSeam:Live(...)`), modules/Diagnostics.lua:369-386 (merges NS.Sim:Status() with NS.SimHost.Status(); the timeline line reads the library status fields pos/total/ready/playing). No provider key is registered twice (C.8 raises on a second owner).
(5) modules/SimScenario.lua keeps SCENARIOS (:71-81) and NAMES, Timeline (:85-115) as each def's pure `timeline(def, opts)`, PLAY (:125-146) as `SC.Play(step, session) -> detail`, `ready` (:288-310) and Start's pool build (:312-327) as `SC.Prepare(session, def, opts, ready)` (calls SimPool.Build with `{ after = function(d, fn) return NS.Sim:After(d, fn) end }` and `ready()` once the pool is built, then roster, Join, ShowWindow), and the step-delay reader (:37-66; DW KEEPS its `sim.stepDelay` setting: C.11's fixed constant binds the new LH/BL simulators, and the library takes a function). defs: key/dungeon/delve/world with no sizes; raid and lfr `sizes = {9, 12, 15, 19}` (SimPanel.lua:62's list without the 0 the library supplies as Random). items.spec:
No commit; recorded in exceptions.tsv with a proving command. Space the two writes out (throttle rule). Labels `bug`, `state:untriaged`, `severity:low` each.
1. Title `ItemRead bonus walk can leave a nil hole and take the modifier offset from an undefined border`. Body: core/ItemRead.lua:54-57 `bonusAndModifiers`: `bonus[i] = int(f[at + i - 1])` can store nil for an empty field, then `at = at + #bonus` advances by the border of a table with a hole, so the modifier count is read from the wrong field. Fix: advance by the declared count `int(f[F_BONUS_COUNT]) or 0`. Addon-local: DW keeps its own walk because it also reads modifiers (LibKa0s Item.BonusIDsFromLink keeps empty fields but returns no modifiers). Test idea: a link with an empty bonus field followed by modifiers.
2. Title `Restriction announce edge omits the combat flag, so PLAYER_REGEN edges may go unannounced under the Combat type`. Body: modules/Restrictions.lua:140-143 `signature` signs reason, canSendChat, canInspect and canTrade only; QuickComms 5a96af0 added `|..inCombat()` for the same defect. Needs the owner's in-client confirmation before a fix.
Skip either if a commit in this run already fixed it (none planned).

items.title: Sim host contract 2/4 (H3): core/Dispatch.lua, one EVENT_ROWS and one HOOK_ROWS table with NS.Deliver/NS.DeliverHook, registration parity proven
smoke: SM-LH-19: regression after the dispatch refactor: one session of normal play (loot, merchant sell and buy, mailbox, auction post, bank deposit) records the same rows as before; /lh disable then /lh enable resumes capture; with gains and losses off only loot rows appear.
items.spec: req-lh-sim.md §3.2-3.3. New core/Dispatch.lua (~120 lines), TOC after core/CoreSetup.lua and above every module (LOAD-BEARING comment). `NS.EVENT_ROWS`: ordered list of `{ event, owner, target, fn }`, target in 'bus'|'out'|'ledger'|'spell', fn(event, ...) receiving the client's full payload; each module appends its rows at file load (the R.SCAN_STEPS precedent, modules/Escrow.lua:20), so row order is TOC order = today's stand-up order (core/LifecycleSetup.lua:177-184): Attribution, AttributionOut, Collector, Reconciler. `NS.RegisterRows(owner, targetObj, targetKey)` registers every matching row via NS.SafeRegisterEvent / SafeRegisterUnitEvent (the spell target is the RegisterUnitEvent frame, Attribution.lua:449-455), setting row.registered = true only on success; `NS.UnregisterRows(owner)` clears it. Each registration's handler is `NS.Deliver(row, event, ...)`, which today is just `return row.fn(event, ...)` plus a single hook point `NS.RealEventFilter` (nil until LH-10; when set and it answers true the event is consumed) so LH-10 adds the real/simulated split without touching this file's callers; cost with no filter is one nil test. `NS.HOOK_ROWS`: ordered `{ name, member?, fn }`, appended at file load by Attribution (5 rows, the LH-06 Compat.HookSecure installs) and AttributionOut (13 rows, :143-162), installed ONCE per session through Compat.HookSecure/HookSecureMember keeping the `_hooked`/`_outHooked` latches and the stood-down gate in the bodies; each installed hook calls `NS.DeliverHook(row, ...)`. BuyMerchantItem keeps its two rows (StampVendor then StampOut BUY) in that order. `NS.DeliverAll(event, ...) -> n` (used by the sim's deliver later): walks EVENT_ROWS in order and pcalls every registered row for `event`, or walks HOOK_ROWS for `hook:<name>`, answering the count.
