items.spec: Build on LibKa0s-Sim-1.0 as landed (docs/api/Sim/ host contract H1-H10, LK-18), with OWNER_SCOPE C binding over design-sim.md: no seam:IsActive/IsGuarded (use NS.Sim:IsActive()), no help verb, one Live (on the seam), RunTo internal, a second SetProvider for a key raises, host fields live on NS.SimHost never on the library instance (C.4), stale ready() ignored (C.1). core/SimSeam.lua (new, ~60 lines), TOC line directly after core/Compat.lua with a LOAD-BEARING comment (H2): `NS.SimSeam = Sim:NewSeam(NS.Compat, { name = 'LootHistory', pure = PURE, guarded = { ListCurrencies = function() return (NS.SimHost.world and NS.SimHost.world.currencies) or {} end } })`; PURE = the text/parse helpers (FoldNBSP, IsAuctionHouseMail, DecodeGUID, BindState, BestBound, CurrencyLinkID, AuctionMailKind, CurrencySourceName, InteractionType), the tooltip Show*/HideTooltip family and the four hook installers (HookUseContainerItem, HookGetQuestReward, HookSecure, HookSecureMember), per req §2.2; everything else is wrapped (answered live until a provider is set in LH-11). Degradation (LibStub('LibKa0s-Sim-1.0', true) nil): wrap nothing and build the inert stub of design-sim.md §7 for both seam and session (IsActive/IsDelivering/IsPanelShown false, Fire/DeliverForCleanup 0, After nil, Start false+line, RunVerb prints 'The simulator needs LibKa0s-Sim-1.0.' and answers false,'absent', Live calls fn, SetProvider/OnStop/OnStopGuarded/AddListener/panel members no-ops, Status {active=false}, Session nil, PanelRows/Steps {}). modules/Sim.lua (new, ~300 lines; TOC after the capture modules, after modules/SimScenario.lua's later slot, above modules/Diagnostics.lua and settings/Schema.lua): `NS.Sim = Sim:New{ name='LootHistory', seam=NS.SimSeam, slash='/lh sim', deliver=NS.DeliverAll (LH-07), isStoodDown=NS.IsStoodDown, scenarios=NS.SimHost.SCENARIOS (filled at file load by LH-12; suites here register a test-only def), prepare, play, refusal, gate, stepDelay=SIM_STEP_DELAY (a fixed file constant, no schema row, C.11), stopText, print=NS.Print, debug=tagged 'Sim', L=NS.L }`. refusal (run inside Live by the library, in this order): stood down; test mode on (NS.BrowserTable.testMode); real combat (Compat.PlayerInCombat); inside any instance (Compat.InInstance); real group (Compat.InGroup); a real interaction frame open (next(State.scopes) or next(R.readable)); ledger settling (R._pending, R._holdSince, R.deferred or R.loginPending); login deferrals not run (not State.cleanupDone or not State.loginSettled); scenario-specific (vendor/ah/bank/social refuse when settings.trackLedger is off: 'these steps record through the ledger, so turn on gains and losses first'). BrowserTable testModeRefusal (:638-645) gains the converse case (test mode refuses while NS.Sim:IsActive()). Start (prepare): create NS.SimHost session fields (world, counters), set NS.SimStores to fresh {history={},holdings={},daily={}} (seed the alt Simalt-<realm> into session holdings), R:ResetState(), Attribution:ResetContexts(), register the private world-watch target, session genesis R:LoginScan() with the seam on (silent genesis), Browser OnDatasetChanged, then ready(). STARTED string overridden with 'Simulation started (%s): nothing is saved; your history and holdings are not touched.' Real-event split: set NS.RealEventFilter (LH-07 hook point) to classify real input while active and not delivering: interference (CHAT_MSG_LOOT/CURRENCY/MONEY when the self-parse matches; LOOT_OPENED, ENCOUNTER_START, CHALLENGE_MODE_START, QUEST_TURNED_IN, TRADE_ACCEPT_UPDATE, MAIL_SEND_SUCCESS, PLAYER_INTERACTION_MANAGER_FRAME_SHOW; any real hook) -> NS.Sim:Stop('world') then deliver live into the real stores; absorbed (bag, money, currency, equipment, bank, auction, spell-cast) -> ignored. World-watch target: GROUP_ROSTER_UPDATE -> Stop('group') when live in a group; PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD / ZONE_CHANGED_NEW_AREA -> Stop('instance') when live in an instance; PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED -> Stop('combat'). Stop: OnStopGuarded none needed; OnStop (seam off), each step isolated by the library: NS.CancelDeferral(R._pending/R._recheck), R:ResetState(), Attribution:ResetContexts(), NS.SimStores fields back to nil, unregister world-watch, NS.After(1, R:LoginScan) unless reason == 'standDown' (real drift becomes UNTRACKED), Browser OnDatasetChanged + HISTORY_CHANGED + HOLDINGS_CHANGED, clear NS.SimHost session fields, one [Sim] debug line (events, rows, reason). items.title: Simulator 3/5: modules/SimScenario.lua, six scenarios as timelines with the ledger-settled gate, plus the end-to-end and saved-data invariant suites
items.spec: req-lh-sim.md §7 and OWNER_SCOPE C.12. modules/SimScenario.lua (~320 lines, TOC above modules/Sim.lua) fills NS.SimHost.SCENARIOS = { names = {'loot','key','vendor','ah','bank','social'}, defs = {...} } with pure `timeline(def, opts) -> steps` (each step a host table with kind, label, the driver calls, and a tip of what it injects) and the `play(step, session)` dispatcher calling SimDrivers. Scenarios and their expected rows exactly as req §7: loot (KILL with npcID detail, GOLD IN KILL, CONTAINER, QUEST, the gated poor item only as a Reconciler diff row, no duplicates whichever of chat or bags arrives first), key (KILL with encounter + keystone detail, MPLUS from the chest, BONUS_ROLL and ROLL as CERTAIN, a currency row under the listed id, keystone context cleared after zone-out; bags change during simulated combat so the flush defers to the regen edge), vendor (item OUT SELL, gold IN SELL, item IN VENDOR, gold OUT BUY, gold OUT REPAIR, item OUT DESTROY, materials DISENCHANT, item OUT DECONSTRUCT), ah (MOVE bags->auctions, gold OUT AH_POST_FEE and AH_BUY, exit held then item OUT AH_SOLD with gold IN AH_SOLD, won item IN AH, expired item back as own-origin MOVE), bank (intra-holder MOVE, WARBAND_DEPOSIT/WITHDRAW pairs, warband genesis on first read), social (OUT ALT_MAIL with the alt credited in the session store, ALT_TRADE both ways, TRADE_GIVE and IN TRADE, CURRENCY_TRANSFER pair rows). Every scenario ends on a settled ledger. Host `gate(session)`: open only when no R._pending, no R._holdSince, no R.deferred (Reconciler debounce 0.35 s, claim wait 1.5 s, one-sided hold 6 s, core/Ledger.lua:49), else `false, L['settling…']`; the library checks it before every Step/Run tick/RunTo. items.title: Perf-hold refusal: Toggle Comms Pads (slash, launcher, key binding), test mode and Preview as... answer the capture line, not the disabled line, under the perf hold alone
smoke: SM-QC-6: start a perf capture from /qc perf's step panel, then press the Toggle Comms Pads key, type /qc toggle and /qc test -> each prints 'Not available during a performance capture.' once and nothing toggles; finish the capture -> the key toggles the pads again
SM-QC-7: /qc disable, press the Toggle Comms Pads key -> the disabled line (unchanged, KEY-3)
items.spec:
Defect (OWNER_SCOPE F, design-std.md:777): settings/SlashVerbs.lua:71 `if NS.IsStoodDown() then return NS.Print(NS.SlashCommands:DisabledLine()) end` prints 'Ka0s Quick Comms is disabled — enable it with /qc enable' during a perf capture, because NS.IsStoodDown() (core/LifecycleSetup.lua:14-16) is true under the `perf` hold too; the dispatcher deliberately gates on the stored switch (settings/Slash.lua:78-83), so the verb reaches the handler and gives wrong advice. The same predicate prints the same wrong line at modules/Preview.lua:46-47 (P.SetTestMode) and :199-200 (P.SetPreviewAs); fix all three so every refusal of the one stand-down speaks by hold (slash-commands-§7 by-hold refusal SHOULD; launcher-§6 MUST: the key press refuses exactly as the toggle does).

CHANGE core/LifecycleSetup.lua: add, after NS.IsStoodDown and before the `if not lib` branch (so the live and stand-in loads both carry it and the NS parity case stays green), DropWatcher's helper verbatim in shape (DropWatcher/core/LifecycleSetup.lua:18-27): `--- Why a stood-down feature refuses, as the one line to print, or nil while standing up...` `function NS.StoodDownRefusal() if not NS.IsStoodDown() then return nil end; if NS.Lifecycle:IsHeld(NS.HOLD_DISABLED) then return NS.SlashCommands:DisabledLine() end; return NS.L["Not available during a performance capture."] end` (NS.HOLD_DISABLED and NS.SlashCommands read at call time). locales/enUS.lua: add `L["Not available during a performance capture."] = "Not available during a performance capture."` (the DW wording). settings/SlashVerbs.lua:71 -> `local refusal = NS.StoodDownRefusal(); if refusal then return NS.Print(refusal) end`; modules/Preview.lua:46-47 and :199-200 -> the same, keeping `return false`. Update the V.TogglePads docblock (:65-69) to say the refusal speaks by hold. Nothing else changes: the disabled hold still prints DisabledLine; the dispatcher gate is unchanged.

TESTS (test-first; each red on the current tree): in tests/test_disabled.lua (the slash-commands-§7 suite) add (1) `disabled [by hold]: under the perf hold alone, /qc toggle refuses with the capture line and leaves padsHidden alone` (Hold NS.HOLD_PERF, m.prints = {}, NS.addon:OnSlashCommand("toggle"), assert one print equal to the capture line, no 'is disabled' text, NS.db.char.padsHidden unchanged; red under: restore SlashVerbs.lua:71); (2) `... the Toggle Comms Pads key press refuses as /qc toggle does` (click m.__named.QuickCommsTogglePads, the test_dial.lua:465-481 pattern; same assertion); (3) `... test mode and Preview as refuse with the capture line` (NS.Preview.SetTestMode(true) and SetPreviewAs("arena") return false, one capture line each); (4) `disabled [by hold]: with both holds the disabled line wins`. tests/test_preview.lua:83-92 (disabled hold) stays unchanged and green. Regenerate docs/test-cases.md, roll README.md:6's badge.

DOCS: docs/slash-dispatch.md:30-32 -> the stored-switch gate sentence stays, and the false claim 'so a perf capture never refuses a verb' becomes: a perf capture never refuses at the dispatcher, but the feature verbs that would act on a stood-down addon (toggle, test, preview, and the Toggle Comms Pads key and the launcher's Show window and Test mode entries through the same handlers) answer `Not available during a performance capture.`; the table rows :14, :22, :23 add 'a perf capture alone: the capture line'. docs/performance.md:11-13 one sentence on that line. docs/module-map.md row 10 (`core/LifecycleSetup.lua`) adds `NS.StoodDownRefusal`. docs/smoke-tests.md: KEY-3 is not rewritten (its pass is recorded); add `**STATE-5. A perf capture refuses by its own line (2026-10-22).**` with SM-QC-6/7's steps, Index `STATE-1..5`, and a `## Pending sign-off` entry (origin OWNER_SCOPE F, owed).

VERIFY: `lua tests/run.lua` all pass, `luacheck .` 0/0; `grep -rn 'IsStoodDown() then' modules settings | grep DisabledLine` returns nothing. Commit `QC-02: refuse by hold: a perf capture answers its own line in toggle, the key binding, test mode and Preview as` (no QuickComms issue to close).

items.title: Record the LibKa0s#49 and #56 rejections where the next author looks: Documented deviations rows for the restriction tracker/readers copy and the IconStyle copy
items.spec:
Docs and comments only, no behaviour. analysis-workflow.json (#49 item 4a addon_adoptions, challenge): QuickComms carries a copy of DropWatcher's restriction tracker (modules/Restrictions.lua, header cites DW) and its four restriction readers (core/Compat.lua:129, :138, :144, :155; :126-127 'copied from DropWatcher core/Compat.lua:215-266'), and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's `## Documented deviations` (:336) has no row pointing at LibKa0s#49, so a future re-check finds only DW's copy (DropWatcher/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:300). The copies have already drifted (QC 5a96af0 signs the full reason set plus a combat flag, QC Restrictions.lua:129-136, against DW's four answers). Likewise modules/IconStyle.lua is a declared DW copy (its header :2-3) and LibKa0s#56 rejected IconStyle.

ADD two rows to the docs/ARCHITECTURE.md Documented deviations table (shape `| Rule | What differs | Why | Decided | Re-check trigger |`, DW :296-300's rule cell): (1) `library-stack-§7, anti-pattern #47` | the restriction tracker (modules/Restrictions.lua: the event hints, chat lockdown and combat folded into CanSendChat, InCombat and ActiveReason, announced on the reason set plus a combat flag) and its four readers (core/Compat.lua InChatMessagingLockdown, RestrictionTypes, IsRestrictionStateActive, IsRestrictionActive) are copied from DropWatcher, not taken from LibKa0s | LibKa0s#49 rejected the tracker (bars 2 and 3: the two copies' announce edges, answer sets and combat-edge ownership differ) and deferred the readers (guards, not readers; first to promote as Compat minor 2), recorded in the standard's open-evolutions index (WS-10) | 2026-10-22 (LibKa0s v1.75.0 run) | the shared trigger, verbatim from the #49 record: a third roster addon (not a copy) needs a restriction answer set; or the DW and QC copies converge on one announce edge and answer set; or a 12.2 patch cycle passes with no change to Enum.AddOnRestrictionType, the event payload or the chat-blocking classification (two of these) |. (2) `library-stack-§7` | modules/IconStyle.lua (the Icons tab's look: Config, ApplyIcon, IconFrame, PaintBorder, PaintRing) and the glow lifecycle in modules/Glow.lua (the sig gate, the proc burst, the triggers) stay in the addon, copied from DropWatcher | LibKa0s#56 promoted only the stateless driver (LibKa0s-Glow-1.0, QC-01) and rejected IconStyle, the lifecycle layer, published defaults/catalogs and the LSM 'Solid' registration | 2026-10-22 | the #56 record's trigger as WS-10 indexes it (e.g. a fourth consumer copies the knob table, or one host edits a range and the others do not) |. Cite the open-evolutions entry by its WowAddonStandards path as WS-10 lands it (read it, do not paraphrase a different trigger).

POINTERS: docs/compat-layer.md:57-59 ('The restriction shims are copied from DropWatcher's core/Compat.lua') gains 'LibKa0s#49 deferred them; see ARCHITECTURE.md Documented deviations'; one comment line each at the header of modules/Restrictions.lua and modules/IconStyle.lua: `-- Kept in-addon: LibKa0s#49 (resp. #56) rejected under library-stack-§7; re-check trigger in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md -> Documented deviations.` (comment-only, analysis #56 IconStyle addon_adoptions).

items.title: launcher-§6: the Show window key binding (Bindings.xml CLICK WhatGroupTogglePopup:LeftButton) on WhatGroup:ToggleFrame, refusing by hold while stood down; test_disabled step 8 extended; docs
smoke: SM-WG-5: Esc > Options > Key Bindings > AddOns > 'Ka0s WhatGroup' lists 'Toggle group popup' with no key preassigned; bind a key
SM-WG-6: press the key with no capture -> the popup opens on its 'No data' fallbacks; press again -> it closes (ESC/Close semantics, test mode ends if on); one press toggles once
SM-WG-7: /wg test, then press the key -> the sample popup closes and test mode ends, as the menu's Show window does
SM-WG-8: /wg disable, press the key -> exactly one chat line 'Ka0s WhatGroup is disabled - enable it with /wg enable', no popup; /wg enable
SM-WG-9: press the key in combat -> it opens/closes exactly as the launcher's Show window does in combat (no ADDON_ACTION_BLOCKED, no taint line); /reload keeps the bound key
items.spec:
Test first. Binding decisions (design-std.md A1 launcher-§6, binding over OWNER_SCOPE F): one CLICK binding, plain named hidden non-secure Button, OnClick calls the handler the launcher's toggleWindow calls (core/LauncherSetup.lua:193 -> WhatGroup:ToggleFrame, modules/Frame.lua:1278), permanent name, no default key, labels from the module through L, a press while stood down refuses by hold.

1. Bindings.xml (NEW, repo root, CRLF per .gitattributes, NOT listed in WhatGroup.toc):
   <Bindings>
   	<!-- comment: the Show window key (launcher-§6); clicks the plain WhatGroupTogglePopup button modules/Frame.lua creates; label set there -->
   	<Binding name="CLICK WhatGroupTogglePopup:LeftButton" header="WHATGROUP" category="ADDONS"/>
   </Bindings>
   No default attribute, no Lua body.

2. core/LifecycleSetup.lua: add NS.StandDownRefusal() beside NS.IsStoodDown (:46, before the 'if not lib' branch so the degraded latch stub answers too): returns nil when not stood down; NS.SlashCommands:DisabledLine() when NS.Lifecycle:IsHeld(NS.HOLD_DISABLED) (disabled wins when both are held); otherwise NS.L['Not available during a performance capture.']. Everything resolved at call time (Slash.lua loads later). This is the addon's one refusal helper (slash-commands-§7 'Which refusal, by hold'); no third wording.

3. locales/enUS.lua: add L['Toggle group popup'] and L['Not available during a performance capture.'] (verbatim, trailing period).

4. modules/Frame.lua, directly after WhatGroup:IsFrameOnScreen (:1290-1292): NS.TOGGLE_BUTTON = 'WhatGroupTogglePopup'; NS.TOGGLE_COMMAND = ('CLICK %s:LeftButton'):format(NS.TOGGLE_BUTTON); a do-block that CreateFrame('Button', NS.TOGGLE_BUTTON, UIParent) with NO template, RegisterForClicks('AnyDown'), SetScript('OnClick', function() local line = NS.StandDownRefusal(); if line then return NS.Print(line) end; NS.addon:ToggleFrame() end), Hide(); BINDING_HEADER_WHATGROUP = 'Ka0s WhatGroup' (brand, launcher-§1); rawset(_G, 'BINDING_NAME_' .. NS.TOGGLE_COMMAND, L['Toggle group popup']). Header comment: launcher-§6, why CLICK on a named frame, why no secure template, why AnyDown, that the name is permanent (renaming unbinds every player's key), and that this load-time frame is NOT the UISpecialFrames taint source (modules/Frame.lua:725-726, :948-952): it is never added to UISpecialFrames. WhatGroup:ToggleFrame itself is unchanged (the launcher menu grays Show window while disabled, so it never needed to refuse). Every later item adds one ruling paragraph to the same changelog entry, and WS-11 numbers them and adds the 'Who is affected' block.

**Measured baseline:**
- master is at 6bb1bc7 (v2.85.0, 2026-10-20). `check-standard.sh` exits 0: 27 section files, anti-patterns #1 to #95, 1860 citations.
- The run branch does not exist in this repo yet; WS-01 creates it.
- The repo has no Lua, so there is no CCN check and no 1500-line cap. Its gate is check-standard.sh, LF only, and a read for meaning.
- check-standard's anti-patterns check forces numbering. #96 must land with the launcher-§6 heading (WS-02) and #97 with the marker rule (WS-03). WS-02 also has to be a single commit, because every `launcher-§6` citation must resolve to the new `### 6.` heading in the same tree.

**Corrections to design-std, from OWNER_SCOPE and what I measured:**
1. **The `__` clause is narrowed.** Design-std's sentence 'a consumer MUST NOT call a `__` member' is dropped. Consumers call these members today. A roster grep outside libs/ and tests/_kit/ found `__PatchLSM30Border` in 12 files, `__panels` in 26, `__AttachCompose` in 4 and `__IsCombatLocked` in 1.
2. **The closed icon set is close, copy, clear, info.** There is no `confirm`. TestStrip and step-panel art are passed in by the host. The sentence 'adding a name is a major decision' is gone.
3. **launcher-§6 does not list addons in its body.** A key press refuses exactly as the toggle does. Choosing the refusal line by hold stays a SHOULD in slash-commands-§7. The step 8 test assertions are worded to match that.
4. **The marker rule covers the explicit Test mode only.** It does not cover unlock-to-preview. Content that names the test, like WhatGroup's 'Test Group', counts as the marker. A display that is minimized with its header hidden is carved out (OWNER_SCOPE D).
5. **TestStrip has no RESERVE member and no library tooltip.**
6. **Glow and Sim adoption is required of none.** A simulator first shipped on v1.75.0 or later MUST be built on Sim-1.0. A host's own LibCustomGlow start/stop code from before adoption is not anti-pattern #47.
7. **The automated-tests-§3 change is a clarification.** `crashedFiles` appears only as a parenthetical.
8. **The file count in design-std is wrong.** It says 17 majors across 39 files, but design-sim D1 puts Sim in three files. The expected count is 17 majors across 41 files if the step panel is public, or 40 or 41 if it is Sim-private. WS-08 recounts at the LibKa0s head and covers both branches. It also corrects 'Options ten' to eleven, adds Media two, and lists the full count ripple: library-stack :82, :108 and :118; anti-patterns :54; open-evolutions :13, :14 and :155; EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY :57; NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT :1358; STANDARDS :57.

A failure mid-way leaves no green intermediate, and C.10's case-by-case porting record becomes hard to review.
problems.fix: Split it in two. DW-02a covers the seam and session (SimSetup, Sim:New, OnStop/OnStopGuarded, the stub with parity, Unwrapped), with SimScenario's machine still driving through the session's Fire and After. DW-02b covers the timeline (prepare, play and the defs on the library, the step machine deleted, the C.1/C.2 cases). Each stays green.

problems.problem: Size risk. One L item combines the seam, the degradation stubs, the session host, ten ordered refusals, the real-event split filter, world-watch, stand-down and profile auto-stops, and refusal guards on five destructive surfaces across Schema.lua, Slash.lua, Reconciler.lua and BrowserTable.lua (BrowserTable.lua is 1302 lines).
problems.fix: Split it in two. LH-10a covers core/SimSeam.lua, the stubs, parity and Unwrapped. LH-10b covers modules/Sim.lua: the session, refusals, auto-stops and destructive-surface guards. Add `wc -l modules/BrowserTable.lua` < 1500 to VERIFY.

problems.fix: Keep only the opts.icon branch: pass NS.Icon("search"), delete MakeSearchMark and SEARCH_INSET*. Drop the fallback branch.

missing_items.title: preview-mode marker: AuraMaster's explicit test mode says so on the display (WS-03, #97)
missing_items.spec:
ADDONS.md lists AuraMaster with an explicit Test mode (NS.State.testMode, modules/Preview.lua:13-27). modules/Container.lua:719-782 shows placeholder auras while it is on, and a locked test mode deliberately draws no box. design-std D says 'AuraMaster: test mode only, no window. Audit its marker.' No item covers it, yet WS-03 makes a visible, localized text marker in every layout a MUST (#97).

The item starts by reading the container render path while test mode is on, locked and unlocked. If no visible text marker exists, add one per container: a localized label such as L['TEST MODE'], anchored to the container and shown only while NS.State.testMode. It must be readable without hover and visible locked or unlocked. It is not a TestStrip, because a container has no filter bar.

Tests, test-first: the marker is shown with test mode on (locked and unlocked), hidden with it off, and its text comes from L.
Docs: docs/smoke-tests.md gets a new row with Result owed. Regenerate docs/test-cases.md and the README badge.
If a marker already satisfies the rule, record AM-01 in exceptions.tsv with a grep proving it.
VERIFY: ka0s-bounded lua tests/run.lua; luacheck . 0/0.
